t: You are on Flaxman Terrace, a street in the London Borough of Camden. It is named after John Flaxman, an English sculptor and draughtsman who was a leading figure in British and European Neoclassicism. Early in his career he worked as a modeller for Josiah Wedgwood's pottery. He then spent several years in Rome, where he produced his first book illustrations. He was also a prolific maker of funerary monuments. So the street carries the name of an artist whose work ranged from pottery designs to memorials.
